claims.text: Stainless steel is prone to corrosion in extreme environments.
Computational-modeling-assisted coating can improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
Surface alloying can improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
Surface modification produces modified surface properties.
The proposed surface modification alters surface chemistry.
The proposed surface modification alters surface microstructure.
Altered surface chemistry and microstructure lead to improved corrosion resistance.
The ability of stainless steel to endure extreme corrosion is reduced at baseline.
Surface modification techniques have limits under the stated conditions.
The effectiveness of computational modeling for predicting optimal surface properties is uncertain.
Failure to observe a significant improvement in corrosion resistance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes computational modeling as assistance for physical coating or surface alloying, whereas the intervention field describes surface modification as being performed using computational modeling itself. Modeling predicts or guides a modification but is not, by itself, a physical surface-modification method.
